body.p: Reconsideration of the Application is respectfully requested. I. Status of the Claims

Claims 24 and 37 are amended herein. Claims 28 and 35 are cancelled. Claims 25-27, 29- 34, 36, and 38-44 are as previously presented. Support for the amendments can be found in the Specification, specifically Paragraphs [0043] and [0044]. No new matter has been added and claims 24-27, 29-34, and 36-44 are pending.
II. Request for Consideration Under AFCP 2.0

In light of Applicant's proposed amendments to the claims in this Response, Applicant hereby requests consideration under the AFCP 2.0 Program and submits the required Request form with this filing. Applicant respectfully submits that any additional search or consideration necessitated by the present claim amendments should be minimal. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that any further search should not be burdensome; and therefore, the Request for consideration under AFCP 2.0 Program should be granted and the claims allowed.
III. All Claims Meet 35 U.S.C. § 112

Claims 24, 35, and 37 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112 as allegedly being indefinite. Claims 24 and 37 have been amended herein and Claim 35 has been cancelled. Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner remove all such rejections.
IV. Double Patenting Rejection

Claims 24-27, 29-33, and 35-36 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness- type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 12-14 and 19 of U.S. Patent No. 11,712,172 to Govari et al. ("Govari '172") in view of US Patent No. 10,441,188 to Katz et al. ("Katz").
Claim 34 is rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claim 12 of Govari '172 in view of Katz.
Claims 37-44 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-3 of Govari '172 in view of Katz.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with Examiner's analysis of the cited reference. Nevertheless, without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, Applicant submits herewith a Terminal Disclaimer with this Response in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321 to overcome this rejection. Accordingly, Applicant submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance and respectfully requests the claims be allowed.
V. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. @ 103

Claims 24-27 and 29-44 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over US Patent Pub. No. 2020/0375489 to Govari ("Govari") in view of Katz. Applicant notes that claim 35 has been cancelled, rendering its rejection moot. Applicant further traverses the rejections.

Applicant submits that Govari is not prior art to the present application. Govari is a reference under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2), since it is a US Patent Publication and did not publish prior to the filing date of the present application. Both Govari and the present application share an inventor (Assaf Govari) and both the present application and Govari are commonly owned by Biosense Webster (Israel) Ltd.. The exceptions under both § 102(b)(2)(A) and (C) apply. Both applications share an inventor and were owned or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same entity not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention.

The Statement Invoking Common Ownership is provided above in this Response and the signing of this Response acts as the signature in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). Further, evidence of common ownership are the filed ADS for both cases. Thus, Govari is disqualified as prior art.

Turning now to Katz, it too is commonly owned by Biosense Webster (Israel) Ltd. but Applicant submits that it qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1), publishing March 14, 2019, less than one year before the effective filing date of the present application. A Statement under 35 U.S.C. §102(b)(1)(A) is not made at this time, as Govari is disqualified as prior art. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that, having disqualified Govari as prior art, all pending claims are in condition for allowance.
VI. Fees

This Response is filed within 3 months of the October 26, 2023 Office Action. Accordingly, no extension of time fees are believed due. No claims fees are believed to be due. No additional fees are believed to be due. Applicant nonetheless authorizes the Commissioner to charge deposit account No. 20-1507 for any fees deemed due to keep the Application pending or credit any overpayment.

It is believed the Application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is respectfully requested to contact the undersigned if there are any remaining issues which can be resolved by a Supplemental or Examiner's Amendment.
